thread:
Alex: heads up — CI on main turned red after the scheduler image bump. kernel-integration-test failing consistently in the new job. anyone around to help bisect? :thinking:
CI Bot: Build failed: https://ci.redwood.infra/builds/BR-98234 (workflow: integration/scheduler). Failed job: kernel-integration-test (run 98234). Logs attached.
Maria: ack, I saw the alert. Last green on main was commit abcdef12 (merge: feature/scheduler-image-bump) — green at 1876500120.
Jordan: I can take a first pass. Any repro steps? Does it fail locally or only on CI?
Alex: failing on CI containers but I can repro inside a dev image with the bumped base. repro steps:
```
# from repo root
git checkout main
git pull
docker build -t redwood/scheduler:test -f docker/scheduler/Dockerfile .
./scripts/run_integration.sh --image redwood/scheduler:test --test kernel-integration --repeat 3
```
It times out waiting for kernel attach on the 2nd test run, log excerpt: 
```
[2026-06-15T03:12:10Z] ERROR kernel-test: timeout waiting for kernel attach (30s)
[2026-06-15T03:12:10Z] ERROR kernel-test: assertion failed: expected 4 shards, got 1
```
Sam: cc @Alex @Maria — PR that bumped the base image is #4128 (owner: @Sam). The bump replaced ubuntu:20.04 -> ubuntu:22.04 and bumped glibc/tooling.
Maria: possible suspects: kernel module version, cgroup defaults, or new systemd behavior. Could be ordering change in udev.
Ellen: can we bisect main quickly? If we can reproduce inside the dev image we can use a scripted bisect that runs the integration script and returns 0/1. I can provision a runner. :computer:
Jordan: I'll start a git bisect locally. plan: git bisect start; git bisect bad HEAD; git bisect good abcdef12; git bisect run ./scripts/ci-bisect-wrapper.sh (wrapper runs the docker build and integration test and exits non-zero on failure).
Alex: wrapper snippet (if useful):
```
#!/bin/bash
set -e
./docker/build-scheduler.sh || exit 125  # skip if build flaky
./scripts/run_integration.sh --image local/scheduler --test kernel-integration --repeat 1 || exit 1
exit 0
```
CI Bot: Triggered rerun: https://ci.redwood.infra/builds/BR-98235 (manual rerun by Jordan).
Jordan: running bisect on a VM now — will post updates. initial bisection narrowed it to a small range (3 commits). suspects: commit 77a1c3d changed cgroup v2 defaults, commit 77a9bff updated scheduler start flags, commit b2d4f88 bumped base image.
Sam: 77a9bff is part of my changes to the startup flags for the scheduler to improve shutdown. It shouldn't affect kernel attach but could change timing. I can add extra logging.
Maria: if bisect points to the base image bump (b2d4f88) we should consider an immediate revert to restore main green while we investigate.
Alex: agreed — prefer an ephemeral revert PR to unblock CI, then deeper fix. Jordan — any early verdict?
Jordan: ok narrowed: good: abcdef12, bad: HEAD, first bad commit reported by bisect-run: 77a9bff. But when I grafted b2d4f88 on top of abcdef12 it failed too — looks like an interaction. so it's an ordering/interaction problem between 77a9bff and b2d4f88.
Ellen: that fits the cgroup/start ordering hypothesis. quick mitigation: revert 77a9bff on main (revert PR) then re-run CI. If that fixes it, we'll land a follow-up that adds a compatibility shim and reapply the flags with a canary.
Sam: I can draft the revert of 77a9bff now. Who should approve? cc @Maria for quick review.
Maria: I can review. also please include a note in the PR body referencing BR-98234 and the CI link.
Alex: sounds good. Also let's add an automated canary test that runs kernel-attach path during PR validation for scheduler changes.
CI Bot: Re-run complete: https://ci.redwood.infra/builds/BR-98236 — kernel-integration-test failing on 77a9bff repro.
Jordan: leaving bisect artifacts here: bisect-log: https://artifacts.redwood.infra/bisect/1876543/bisect.log — contains the script output and the failing test traces.
Sam: created PR #4130 (revert: 77a9bff) — draft. tagging @Maria.
Maria: reviewing now. quick suggestion: add a revert-changelog entry and mention we will re-land after adding startup ordering test.
Ellen: I'll queue the revert PR for staging once it's approved. Can monitor the integration pipeline.
Alex: thanks everyone. once revert lands I'll watch for main green and then we can schedule a follow-up investigation to make the scheduler flags robust across base-image changes. :thumbsup:
Sam: noted, will include test plan in the follow-up.
Jordan: one small follow-up — I captured a minimal repro container diff that demonstrates the timing change. I'll upload to the artifact link in an hour.
Alex: perfect. appreciate the quick turn.
Ellen: marking this thread as tracked for rollback readiness.
Alex: closing for now — will reopen if CI stays red after revert. thanks all :pray:
